paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: a crowd saying yes is not the same as God saying yes. Ahab had four hundred prophets all saying, "Go up and triumph," and he had exactly one man who wouldn't just say what the king wanted. Ahab said it right out loud: he hated Micaiah because he "never prophesies anything good for me, but only bad" (1 Kings 22:8). Ahab was not looking for the truth. He was shopping for a YES.

Now look at Micaiah. The messenger told him to speak favorably like everybody else, and Micaiah answered, "As surely as the LORD lives, I will speak whatever the LORD tells me" (1 Kings 22:13-14). Then he told Ahab about a lying spirit in the mouths of those prophets and about disaster coming, and a prophet struck him in the face and the king threw him in prison (1 Kings 22:23-27). I think that part is heavy, and I think it cost him. But Micaiah stood there and said, "If you ever return safely, the LORD has not spoken through me" (1 Kings 22:28). That is a man who cared more about what God said than what the room wanted.

So here's the question for you, baker: whose voice do you listen to most? It's easy to go looking for the voices that say what we already want to hear, and trust me, there are plenty of them. The Word of God is the one voice worth checking everything else against, so keep your ovens warm and keep reading it for yourself. And stay put, because this story is NOT done.
